In [[differential geometry]], a field in [[mathematics]], a '''natural bundle''' is any [[fiber bundle]] associated to the higher order [[frame bundle]] <math>F^r(M)</math>, for some <math>r \geq 1</math>. In other words, its transition functions depend functionally on local changes of coordinates in the base manifold <math>M</math> together with their partial derivatives up to order at most <math>r</math>.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|title=Natural bundles have finite order|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0040938377900088|journal=[[Topology (journal)|Topology]]|date=1977-01-01|issn=0040-9383|pages=271–277|volume=16|issue=3|doi=10.1016/0040-9383(77)90008-8|first=Richard S.|last=Palais|first2=Chuu-Lian|last2=Terng|author-link1=Richard Palais|author-link2=Chuu-Lian Terng|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

The concept of a natural bundle was introduced in 1972 by [[Albert Nijenhuis]] as a modern reformulation of the classical concept of an arbitrary bundle of geometric objects.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Natural bundles and their general properties|author=Albert|publisher=[[Books Kinokuniya|Kinokuniya]]|year=1972|pages=317–334|location=Tokyo|author-link=Albert Nijenhuis|first=Nijenhuis|url=https://dmitripavlov.org/scans/nijenhuis-natural-bundles-and-their-general-properties.pdf|work=Differential Geometry (in honor of Kentaro Yano)}}</ref>

== Definition ==
Let <math>\mathcal{M}f</math> denote the [[Category of manifolds|category of smooth manifolds]] and [[Smooth map|smooth maps]] and <math>\mathcal{M}f_n</math> the [[Category (mathematics)|category]] of smooth <math>n</math>-dimensional manifolds and [[Local diffeomorphism|local diffeomorphisms]]. Consider also the category <math>\mathcal{FM}</math> of [[Fibered manifold|fibred manifolds]] and bundle morphisms, and the functor <math>B: \mathcal{FM} \to \mathcal{M}f </math> associating to any fibred manifold its base manifold.

A natural bundle (or bundle functor) is a [[functor]] <math>F: \mathcal{M}f_n \to \mathcal{FM}</math> satisfying the following three properties:

# <math>B \circ F = \mathrm{id}</math>, i.e. <math>F(M)</math> is a fibred manifold over <math>M</math>, with projection denoted by <math>p_M: F(M) \to M </math>;
# if <math>U \subseteq M</math> is an open [[submanifold]], with inclusion map <math>i: U \hookrightarrow M</math>, then <math>F(U)</math> coincides with <math>p_M^{-1}(U) \subseteq F(M)</math>, and <math>F(i): F(U) \to F(M)</math> is the inclusion <math> p^{-1}(U) \hookrightarrow F(M)</math>;
# for any smooth map <math>f: P \times M \to N</math> such that <math>f (p, \cdot): M \to N</math> is a local diffeomorphism for every <math>p \in P</math>, then the function <math>P \times F(M) \to F(N), (p,x) \mapsto F(f (p,\cdot)) (x)</math> is smooth.

As a consequence of the first condition, one has a [[natural transformation]] <math>p: F \to \mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{M}f_n}</math>.

== Finite order natural bundles ==
A natural bundle <math>F: \mathcal{M}f_n \to \mathcal{FM}</math> is called of '''finite order''' <math>r</math> if, for every local diffeomorphism <math>f: M \to N</math> and every point <math>x \in M</math>, the map <math>F(f)_x: F(M)_{x} \to F(N)_{f(x)}</math> depends only on the [[Jet (mathematics)|jet]] <math>j^r_x f</math>. Equivalently, for every local diffeomorphisms <math>f,g: M \to N</math> and every point <math>x \in M</math>, one has<math display="block">j^r_x f = j^r_x g \Rightarrow F(f)|_{F(M)_x} =  F(g)|_{F(M)_x}.</math>Natural bundles of order <math>r</math> coincide with the associated fibre bundles to the <math>r</math>-th order [[Frame bundle|frame bundles]] <math>F^r(M)</math>.

After various intermediate cases,<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Natural Vector Bundles and Natural Differential Operators|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2373910|journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]]|date=1978|issn=0002-9327|pages=775–828|volume=100|issue=4|doi=10.2307/2373910|first=Chuu Lian|last=Terng|author-link=Chuu-Lian Terng|url-access=subscription}}</ref> it was proved by [[David B. A. Epstein|Epstein]] and [[William Thurston|Thurston]] that all natural bundles have finite order.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Epstein |first1=D. B. A. |author-link1=David B. A. Epstein |last2=Thurston |first2=W. P. |author-link2=William Thurston |date=1979 |title=Transformation Groups and Natural Bundles |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1112/plms/s3-38.2.219 |journal=[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]] |language=en |volume=s3-38 |issue=2 |pages=219–236 |doi=10.1112/plms/s3-38.2.219|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Natural <math>\Gamma</math>-bundles ==
The notion of natural <math>\Gamma</math>-bundle arises from that of natural bundle by restricting to the suitable categories of [[Pseudogroup#Pseudogroups of symmetries and geometric structures|<math>\Gamma</math>-manifolds]] and of <math>\Gamma</math>-fibred manifolds, where <math>\Gamma</math> is a [[pseudogroup]]. The case when <math>\Gamma</math> is the pseudogroup of all diffeomorphisms between open subsets of <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> recovers the ordinary notion of natural bundle.

Under suitable assumptions, natural <math>\Gamma</math>-bundles have finite order as well.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Bundle functors on fibred manifolds|url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00776852|journal=Annals of Global Analysis and Geometry|date=1991|issn=0232-704X|pages=129–143|volume=9|issue=2|doi=10.1007/BF00776852|language=en|first=Jan|last=Slovák|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Natural Operations in Differential Geometry|url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-662-02950-3|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|date=1993|location=Berlin, Heidelberg|isbn=978-3-642-08149-1|doi=10.1007/978-3-662-02950-3|language=en|first=Ivan|last=Kolář|first2=Jan|last2=Slovák|first3=Peter W.|last3=Michor}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Fibrés naturels sur la catégorie des Γ-variétés|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02844245|journal=Rendiconti del Circolo Matematico di Palermo Series 2|date=1994-09-01|issn=1973-4409|pages=309–328|volume=43|issue=3|doi=10.1007/BF02844245|language=fr|first=Mohamed|last=Benalili|trans-title=Natural bundles on the category of Γ-manifolds|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Examples ==
An example of natural bundle (of first order) is the [[tangent bundle]] <math>TM</math> of a manifold <math>M</math>.

Other examples include the [[Cotangent bundle|cotangent bundles]], the bundles of [[Metric tensor|metrics]] of [[Metric signature|signature]] <math>(r,s)</math> and the bundle of [[Linear connection|linear connections]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Fatibene |first1=Lorenzo |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-94-017-2384-8 |title=Natural and Gauge Natural Formalism for Classical Field Theorie |last2=Francaviglia |first2=Mauro |author-link2=Mauro Francaviglia |date=2003 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-1-4020-1703-2 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-94-017-2384-8}}</ref>
